top_news.title: Israeli opposition leader Eisenkot accuses Netanyahu of delegitimising election results amid Shin Bet probe
top_news.summary: Amid growing political tensions surrounding potential external meddling in the electoral process in Israel, Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the opposition Yashar party, launched a scathing attack against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. According to The Times of Israel, Eisenkot accused the premier of running an organised campaign to undermine the election outcome based on unverified claims, vowing that the scheduled opening of parliament would proceed without delay. Addressing the nation following briefings with security and electoral chiefs, Eisenkot detailed his discussions regarding the unfolding situation. I met earlier with the Shin Bet chief and the head of the Central Elections Committee. I was updated by them on the situation. It is too early to understand what happened and if it happened at all. We must allow the relevant professionals to complete their investigation without any political interference, he said. The opposition leader raised serious concerns regarding external actions, particularly pointing fingers at Doha. Foreign interference in Israel is unacceptable and grave, all the more so when it involves a state that funds terrorism and supports the terrorist organisation Hamas, and which has managed, in recent years, to infiltrate the office of the Prime Minister of Israel, he said, in reference to Qatar. It is essential to investigate whether they tried to exert influence, and through whom they sought to do so, he added. Shifting his focus to domestic political manoeuvres, Eisenkot alleged that the ruling faction was attempting to manipulate the outcome due to a lack of parliamentary backing. What is already clear is that Likud and Netanyahu have embarked on an orchestrated and organised campaign to delegitimise the election results, Eisenkot charged. Their statements and talking points were ready. They are doing this because they lost. They do not have a majority. The State of Israel is governed by the rule of law. I will not allow even a centimetre's deviation from the swearing-in of the Knesset as planned, Eisenkot declared. Reaching out to the working public and security personnel, the opposition figure outlined upcoming legislative priorities intended to reshape governance and accountability. From here, I wish to address the public that serves in the military and works, those determined to live in the State of Israel as a Jewish and democratic, liberal, strong, and secure state, he continued. In the offices here, next to me, teams are already at work finalising preparations for a law on conscription and service for all Israeli citizens, the establishment of a State Commission of Inquiry into the October 7 massacre, legislation to reform the budgetary mechanism, measures to prioritise those who serve, and more, Eisenkot said. The programmes are ready, and in coordination with my partners, we will work to bring them to a vote at the opening of the Knesset. It is my intention to work to fortify and defend the interests of those who work, those who enlist, and those who are committed to the values of the Declaration of Independence, he added. Emphasising a definitive break from past administrative policies, Eisenkot's promise highlighted the intent to redirect state institutions towards public welfare rather than political preservation. articles.title: Israeli opposition leader Eisenkot accuses Netanyahu of delegitimising election results amid Shin Bet probe
articles.summary: Amid growing political tensions surrounding potential external meddling in the electoral process in Israel, Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the opposition Yashar party, launched a scathing attack against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. According to The Times of Israel, Eisenkot accused the premier of running an organised campaign to undermine the election outcome based on unverified claims, vowing that the scheduled opening of parliament would proceed without delay. Addressing the nation following briefings with security and electoral chiefs, Eisenkot detailed his discussions regarding the unfolding situation. I met earlier with the Shin Bet chief and the head of the Central Elections Committee. I was updated by them on the situation. It is too early to understand what happened and if it happened at all. We must allow the relevant professionals to complete their investigation without any political interference, he said. The opposition leader raised serious concerns regarding external actions, particularly pointing fingers at Doha. Foreign interference in Israel is unacceptable and grave, all the more so when it involves a state that funds terrorism and supports the terrorist organisation Hamas, and which has managed, in recent years, to infiltrate the office of the Prime Minister of Israel, he said, in reference to Qatar. It is essential to investigate whether they tried to exert influence, and through whom they sought to do so, he added. Shifting his focus to domestic political manoeuvres, Eisenkot alleged that the ruling faction was attempting to manipulate the outcome due to a lack of parliamentary backing. What is already clear is that Likud and Netanyahu have embarked on an orchestrated and organised campaign to delegitimise the election results, Eisenkot charged. Their statements and talking points were ready. They are doing this because they lost. They do not have a majority. The State of Israel is governed by the rule of law. I will not allow even a centimetre's deviation from the swearing-in of the Knesset as planned, Eisenkot declared.
